how_it_wins:
Start with the number that defines this deck: zero. That is what the engine costs. Edgar Markov's eminence triggers from the command zone — every other Vampire spell you cast makes a 1/1 black Vampire token while he sits at home, untaxed and untouchable. The goldfish run (seed 42, 10,000 iterations, conservative — no interaction modeled) shows what that buys: 1.9 bodies by turn 3, 4.2 by turn 6, on a curve that stacks 8 one-drops and 19 each at two and three. You are the beatdown by default, and unlike most beatdown decks you rebuild after a sweeper at the price of simply casting your next Vampire.

Going wide is not the whole plan, because roughly 120 combined life does not fall to 1/1s. The deck's honest reach is the each-opponent drain: Sanctum Seeker converts every attacking Vampire into 1 life from each opponent, and Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles opponents' life loss on your turn. Stack 003 verified the arithmetic: seven attacking Vampires drain each opponent for 14 at declare-attackers — before blockers exist — and a 14-life opponent is simply eliminated by the trigger stack. A drain engine is drawn by turn 6 in 62.5% of games; a lord or Vampire payoff in 67.7%. Layer a token doubler (42.4% by turn 6) and stack 002's math kicks in: one two-mana Vampire cast becomes five bodies through Anointed Procession and Mondrak.

Edgar himself is the pivot, not the opener. His goldfish median cast is turn 6 (mean 6.613, 52.1% by turn 6), and the correct pivot is casting him the turn you alpha-strike: his attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control, converting an accumulated token board into lethal width. Hold protection for exactly that turn — Akroma's Will, Boros Charm, Flawless Maneuver; the goldfish holds a protection piece by turn 6 in 57.1% of games — and remember the tension the strategic frame names: Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free only while you control a commander, which is precisely what the eminence plan delays.

The infinites are insurance, not plan A. Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose plus either gain-on-loss half — Exquisite Blood or Bloodthirsty Conqueror — is a verified, deterministic table-kill (stacks 001 and 004, both checker-passed), but natural assembly is 2.8% by turn 6 and 4.9% by turn 10. What changes the math is the tutor suite: Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor, and Diabolic Intent are not modeled by the goldfish, and at a bracket-4 floor the table will play as though the combo is coming regardless. Beat down, drain wide, and keep the knockout in your pocket for the game that goes long.

combo_lines.001: The deck's bracket-4 backbone, verified end to end against the June 19, 2026 comprehensive rules over a 10-step resolution. The scene: Exquisite Blood and Vito on your battlefield, and Vampire Nighthawk's lifelink has just gained you 2 off combat damage. That 2-life seed is all the loop needs. Vito's trigger drains a target opponent, Exquisite Blood gains it back, Vito triggers again — and because each Vito trigger is a new object whose target you choose fresh as it goes on the stack, you walk the drain across the table in any order. The checker confirmed the parts people argue about: the loop is shortcut-legal, a targeted opponent dying mid-loop does not break the chain (their killing life loss still triggers your enchantment, which targets nothing), and from this board it takes exactly 38 Vito resolutions — 6, 13, and 19 — to clear opponents at 12, 25, and 38 life. You end at 105 life, having spent no mana and no cards, and win by rule 104.2a the moment the last opponent leaves.
combo_lines.002: The token-math stack, and the one to internalize because it runs every turn, not just combo turns. You cast Gifted Aetherborn for {B}{B} with Edgar still in the command zone and both doublers out. Eminence triggers once — one token event — and Anointed Procession and Mondrak each double it in whichever order you like (the checker confirmed the result is identical: 1 becomes 2 becomes 4). Those four 1/1s each enter carrying a Vampire Socialite counter because an opponent lost life this turn, and the Aetherborn itself arrives as a 3/4. Net: five new Vampire bodies off one two-mana spell. Just as important is what does not happen: eminence does not re-trigger on the tokens (they are created, not cast), and Cordial Vampire stays silent because nothing died. This is the multiplication table behind the goldfish's body counts — know it cold before you commit to a doubler turn.
combo_lines.003: The drain math that makes go-wide combat real against three opponents, verified at the moment of declare-attackers. Seven Vampires attack — Bloodletter, Sanctum Seeker, four eminence tokens, and a hasty Edgar — and Sanctum Seeker triggers once per attacking Vampire: seven triggers. It is your turn, so Bloodletter's replacement doubles each opponent's loss per trigger event: every opponent loses 2, seven times, for 14 total. Your gain is not doubled — Bloodletter reads opponents' life loss only — so you gain 7. The checker confirmed the brutal part: the opponent at 14 hits exactly 0 on the seventh trigger and is eliminated by state-based actions before blockers are ever declared, and because you control the remaining triggers, an opponent's death never strands them. Edgar's own attack trigger has already put a counter on all seven bodies. This is 14 damage per opponent for the cost of turning creatures sideways.
combo_lines.004: The second infinite, verified on its own terms rather than by analogy — the strategic frame insisted, and it was right to. Bloodthirsty Conqueror's trigger matches Exquisite Blood's word for word, and the checker confirmed its '(Damage causes loss of life.)' parenthetical is reminder text, not a damage requirement: Vito's direct life loss triggers it just fine. From a 3-life seed the loop runs exactly as stack 001 did — deterministic, shortcut-legal, retargetable each iteration, unbroken by a mid-loop death — and kills a 9-life and a 30-life opponent in 13 Vito resolutions with zero overkill, leaving you at 60. The honest cost is the difference: Conqueror is a 5/5 creature, and every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed creature removal as a loop-breaker, making this pairing strictly more fragile than the enchantment version. Its flying and deathtouch contribute nothing to the loop — they are for the fair game this card also happens to dominate.

card_roles.Edgar Markov: The engine that never needs to be cast: eminence makes a 1/1 Vampire per other Vampire spell from the command zone, all game, for free. When he does arrive (goldfish median turn 6), cast him as the alpha-strike pivot — his attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control, and first strike plus haste means he leads the charge the turn he lands.
card_roles.Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose: The hinge of both verified infinites (stacks 001 and 004): every life gain becomes targeted life loss. Even without a combo half, he converts each lifelink hit and Sanctum Seeker gain into damage, and his activated ability grants the whole team lifelink for one drain-everything combat.
card_roles.Exquisite Blood: The enchantment half of stack 001's verified table-kill with Vito, and the more resilient of the two gain-on-loss pieces — no creature removal touches it. Fair-game mode: every point of drain your engines inflict comes back as life.
card_roles.Bloodthirsty Conqueror: The creature half of stack 004's verified infinite with Vito — same loop, but exposed to creature removal every iteration. As a fair card it is a 5/5 flying deathtouch body that turns every opponent life loss into gain, which Vito then weaponizes.
card_roles.Sanctum Seeker: The go-wide payoff stack 003 verified: each attacking Vampire drains every opponent for 1 and gains you 1. Seven attackers under Bloodletter is 14 from each opponent before blocks — this is the card that makes token combat scale against three life totals.
card_roles.Bloodletter of Aclazotz: Doubles every opponent's life loss on your turn — drains, combat damage, edict aftermath, all of it. Stack 003 shows the effect: it turned seven Sanctum Seeker triggers into 14 per opponent at declare-attackers.
card_roles.Twilight Prophet: With the city's blessing (trivial here), every upkeep reveals the top card, drains each opponent for its mana value, and puts it in your hand — card advantage and reach in one body, and every gain is a Vito trigger.
card_roles.Bontu's Monument: Cost reducer for the deck's 35 black creature spells that also drains each opponent for 1 (and gains you 1 — a Vito trigger) on every creature cast. On a 19-and-19 two/three-drop curve, the discount is real velocity.
card_roles.Legion Lieutenant: The cleanest lord: other Vampires get +1/+1, turning eminence 1/1s into 2/2s for two mana.
card_roles.Stromkirk Captain: Lord plus first strike for the whole tribe — the card that lets 2/2 tokens trade up and lets your swarm play defense against faster aggro seats.
card_roles.Captivating Vampire: A lord with a lategame mode: tap five Vampires (tokens gladly) to steal the table's best creature permanently — and it becomes a Vampire under your lords.
card_roles.Bloodline Keeper // Lord of Lineage: A token per turn from the tap ability, and at five Vampires — easy with eminence — it transforms into a 5/5 flying +2/+2 lord that keeps making 2/2 fliers.
card_roles.Drana, Liberator of Malakir: First strike means her combat damage lands early, putting a +1/+1 counter on every attacking creature before regular damage is even dealt — a mid-combat anthem on a 2/3 flying body.
card_roles.Vampire Socialite: In this deck an opponent has nearly always lost life, so every later Vampire enters with an extra counter — stack 002's four tokens arrived as 2/2s because of her. Menace makes her a fine early attacker to switch the ability on.
card_roles.Cordial Vampire: Every creature death — yours, theirs, anyone's — puts a counter on each Vampire you control. Alongside Grave Pact and your own edict effects, board wipes aimed at you leave the survivors bigger.
card_roles.Shared Animosity: Every attacker shares a type with every other attacker here, so each one gets +1/+0 per fellow attacker — width converted directly into power. Seven attackers is +6 apiece.
card_roles.Stensia Masquerade: First strike for all attackers plus a permanent +1/+1 counter each time a Vampire connects — the swarm snowballs every combat, and madness lets a discard outlet cast it at a discount.
card_roles.Blade of the Bloodchief: Two +1/+1 counters on the equipped Vampire per creature death, anywhere. On a deathtouch body or under Grave Pact it grows absurdly fast for a one-mana artifact.
card_roles.Akroma's Memorial: The deck's lone seven-drop: flying, first strike, vigilance, trample, haste, and protection from black and red for the whole board — a one-card alpha-strike enabler that also blanks most of the table's removal colours in combat.
card_roles.Vanquisher's Banner: Name Vampire: an anthem plus a card for every Vampire spell you cast — with the curve's cheap casts, it refills as fast as you deploy.
card_roles.Cover of Darkness: Choose Vampire and the swarm gains fear — blockable only by artifact and/or black creatures. The card that turns a stalled board into lethal width.
card_roles.Akroma's Will: The premier swing-turn spell: with Edgar on the battlefield (command zone does not count) you take both modes — flying, vigilance, double strike AND lifelink, indestructible, protection from each colour. Every lifelink point is a Vito trigger.
card_roles.Anointed Procession: Token doubler number one, verified in stack 002: with Mondrak also out, each eminence trigger makes four tokens instead of one. It doubles Black Market Connections' Treasures and Strefan's Blood too.
card_roles.Mondrak, Glory Dominus: Token doubler number two from stack 002, on a 4/4 body that can buy itself an indestructible counter by sacrificing two spare tokens — a doubler that survives the sweeper it invites.
card_roles.Mavren Fein, Dusk Apostle: A free lifelink token every combat your nontoken Vampires attack — steady width, and the lifelink token's gains feed Vito and Ocelot Pride.
card_roles.Ocelot Pride: You gain life constantly here, so this makes a Cat every end step — and with the city's blessing it then copies every token that entered this turn. After an eminence-heavy turn, that clause is a second token doubler.
card_roles.Ivora, Insatiable Heir: Blood tokens on entry and on combat damage, growing with each discard — a cheap aggressive body whose Blood feeds Strefan's attack ability and converts dead cards into draws.
card_roles.Strefan, Maurer Progenitor: Your drains make every player lose life, so Strefan banks multiple Blood tokens per turn cycle — then his attack cashes two of them to put a Vampire from hand onto the battlefield tapped, attacking, and indestructible. Bloodletter and Conqueror love arriving free.
card_roles.Preacher of the Schism: Attacks into the life leader for a lifelink token, or — once your drains put you on top — draws a card per attack instead. A deathtouch 2/4 that opponents hate blocking either way.
card_roles.Welcoming Vampire: A card per turn whenever another power-2-or-less creature enters — every eminence token switches it on. One of the deck's steadiest draw engines (a draw engine is held by turn 6 in 49.8% of goldfish runs).
card_roles.Black Market Connections: The premium life-priced engine: Treasure, cards, or a 3/2 changeling — which is a Vampire, so it counts for lords and Sanctum Seeker. Life is cheap early currency in a deck that gains it back by the dozen.
card_roles.Bloodghast: Sweeper insurance and edict fodder that returns on every landfall — including fetch activations. It can't block, so spend it freely on Diabolic Intent and Grave Pact math.
card_roles.Knight of the Ebon Legion: The best one-drop in the tribe: a pump activation to trade up, and a free +1/+1 counter every end step someone lost 4 or more life — a bar this deck's drains clear constantly.
card_roles.Vampire of the Dire Moon: One mana, deathtouch, lifelink: an early attacker deterrent whose every connected point is a Vito trigger.
card_roles.Vampire Interloper: A 2/1 flier for two that can't block — pure eminence fuel and one more attacking Vampire for Sanctum Seeker triggers.
card_roles.Gifted Aetherborn: Two mana for a 2/3 deathtouch lifelink wall that attacks well under lords — stack 002's demonstration cast, arriving as a 3/4 with Socialite out.
card_roles.Vampire Nighthawk: The classic 2/3 flying deathtouch lifelink — it seeded stack 001's loop with a 2-point lifelink hit, which is all Vito and Exquisite Blood ever need.
card_roles.Nighthawk Scavenger: Nighthawk's bigger sibling: power equal to 1 plus the card types in opponents' graveyards, usually a 4-6 power flying deathtouch lifelinker by the mid-game.
card_roles.Henrika Domnathi // Henrika, Infernal Se: A modal engine: each-player edict, draw, or transform into a 3/4 flying deathtouch lifelink body that pumps your evasive attackers. Take the sacrifice mode while your board is tokens and theirs is one big threat.
card_roles.Voldaren Pariah // Abolisher of Bloodlin: Three spare tokens flip her into a 6/5 flier that forces a target opponent to sacrifice three creatures of their choice — a one-sided board attack madness can cast at a discount.
card_roles.Sorin, Imperious Bloodlord: The -3 cheats Bloodletter or Bloodthirsty Conqueror onto the battlefield on turn three; until then, +1 hands a Vampire deathtouch, lifelink, and a counter, or sacrifices a token for 3 damage and 3 life — which is also a Vito trigger.
card_roles.Grave Pact: Every token death forces each opponent to sacrifice a creature — with eminence bodies as fuel, this is a repeatable table-wide edict engine, and Cordial Vampire grows the team off the same deaths.
card_roles.Swords to Plowshares: Premium one-mana exile; the life their creature's controller gains is a fair price for answering the table's best threat.
card_roles.Path to Exile: The second one-mana exile; the basic land it hands over matters less than the threat it removes.
card_roles.Despark: Two mana to exile any permanent at mana value four or more — the answer to the doublers, wraths-on-a-stick, and commanders the deck otherwise can't touch.
card_roles.Fracture: Two mana, instant speed, kills an artifact, enchantment, or planeswalker — the flexible answer slot for stax pieces and problem enchantments.
card_roles.Rite of Oblivion: Sacrifice a spare token to exile any nonland permanent — twice, with flashback. Eminence makes the additional cost nearly free.
card_roles.Winds of Abandon: Spot exile early, one-sided board wipe on overload late — the deck's clean answer to opposing swarms that leaves your own board untouched.
card_roles.Olivia's Wrath: The asymmetric sweeper: every non-Vampire gets -X/-X where X is your Vampire count. With a wide board it wipes the table and misses your entire army.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: The scalable sweeper: pay life to set X. It hits your own team too, so size it to kill their board while your lords keep the counters-and-anthems survivors alive — or just reset a board you can rebuild faster than anyone.
card_roles.Boros Charm: Three modes, one you'll cast most: permanents you control gain indestructible — the two-mana answer to the sweeper your token board invites. Four to the face closes games the drains started.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Free indestructible — but only while you control a commander, which means it costs a real {2}{W} for every turn Edgar stays home. Budget for that tension; it's the deck's central protection trade-off.
card_roles.Deflecting Swat: Free redirection under the same commander condition as Flawless Maneuver: once Edgar is out, it bounces removal off your combo pieces or steals a tutor. Before then, it's a three-mana trick.
card_roles.Teferi's Protection: The total out: life locked, protection from everything, board phased out. It beats any wrath, any combo turn pointed at you, and any lethal swing — hold it for the disaster, not the inconvenience.
card_roles.Swiftfoot Boots: Hexproof and haste for one to equip — Edgar swings the turn he lands, protected, which is exactly the pivot the strategic frame says to build.
card_roles.Demonic Tutor: The best tutor ever printed, and the card that turns a 4.9%-by-turn-10 natural infinite into a line you choose. It fetches whichever combo half — or answer — the game demands.
card_roles.Vampiric Tutor: Top-of-library tutoring at instant speed for one mana and 2 life — set up the combo half or the sweeper the turn before you need it.
card_roles.Diabolic Intent: Demonic Tutor priced at one creature — and eminence prints the currency. Sacrificing a token to find a combo half is this deck's cleanest exchange rate.
card_roles.Night's Whisper: Two cards for two mana and 2 life — efficient fuel, with the life loss trivially recouped by the drain suite.
card_roles.Sol Ring: The format's fastest start; a turn-one Ring is two extra mana toward double-spelling Vampires every turn after.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: Any Mardu colour, no drawback — the premium rock in a three-colour, colour-hungry deck.
card_roles.Talisman of Indulgence: Black or red on demand at a point of pain, colourless for free — a rock that prioritizes the deck's heaviest pip colours.
card_roles.Nomad Outpost: All three colours, enters tapped — the ingestion fix recorded in HISTORY.md: it replaced Crosis's Catacombs, whose blue identity was illegal under Edgar.
card_roles.Savai Triome: The other tapped tri-land, with a late-game upgrade: cycle it for a card when the mana is settled.
card_roles.Luxury Suite: Untapped black-red with two or more opponents — a free dual in every Commander game.
card_roles.Spectator Seating: Untapped red-white in multiplayer — same deal as Luxury Suite, no cost in practice.
card_roles.Vault of Champions: Untapped white-black in multiplayer — the third bond land, covering the deck's heaviest colour pair.
card_roles.Blood Crypt: Shock land: pay 2 life for untapped black-red the turn it matters. This deck buys life back with interest.
card_roles.Godless Shrine: Shock land for the deck's core white-black pair — pay the 2 when the curve demands it.
card_roles.Sacred Foundry: The red-white shock — least-taxed of the three, since red is only 9 pips deep here.
card_roles.Arid Mesa: Fetches Mountain or Plains duals — and every fetch activation is a landfall trigger for Bloodghast.
card_roles.Bloodstained Mire: Fetches Swamp or Mountain types, including the shocks — fixing plus a free Bloodghast return.
card_roles.Marsh Flats: Fetches Plains or Swamp types — the fetch aimed at the deck's most important colour pair.
card_roles.Prismatic Vista: Fetches any basic untapped — with only five basics, crack it early while targets remain.
card_roles.Caves of Koilos: Painless colourless or white-black at 1 damage — reliable early, cheap late.
card_roles.Battlefield Forge: The red-white painland: colourless for free, coloured at a point.
card_roles.Sulfurous Springs: The black-red painland — one damage is nothing next to what the drains recoup.
card_roles.Concealed Courtyard: Untapped white-black through the first three land drops — exactly when the 8-one-drop, 19-two-drop curve needs it.
card_roles.Haunted Ridge: Black-red, untapped once you control two other lands — a mid-game dual that rarely costs tempo.
card_roles.Shattered Sanctum: White-black on the same two-other-lands condition — untapped in the turns that matter.
card_roles.Sundown Pass: Red-white with the two-other-lands clause — the least-stressed pair, so the occasional tapped turn is fine.
card_roles.Blazemire Verge: Black, or red if you control a Swamp or Mountain — in this manabase, effectively an untapped dual from turn two.
card_roles.Bleachbone Verge: Black, or white with a Plains or Swamp about — same low-cost dual design, aimed at the core pair.
card_roles.Silent Clearing: White or black at a life, and when the game floods, sacrifice it for a card — a land that never goes dead.
card_roles.Sunbaked Canyon: The red-white horizon land: pain mana early, a fresh card late.
card_roles.Mana Confluence: Any colour at 1 life per tap — the best fixing in the deck, priced in a resource the drains replenish.
card_roles.Reflecting Pool: Any type your other lands could produce — with this many duals and tri-lands, it is a painless rainbow.
card_roles.Ancient Tomb: Two colourless at 2 damage — a turn-one Tomb into a two-drop plus eminence token is one of the deck's fastest openings.
card_roles.Castle Locthwain: Black mana that becomes a life-priced draw engine when your hand empties — and this curve empties hands fast.
card_roles.Minas Tirith: White mana, usually untapped (fourteen legendary creatures here), that draws a card whenever you attacked with two or more creatures — a bar this deck clears every combat.
card_roles.Cori Mountain Monastery: Red mana with a late-game impulse draw stapled on — four mana for an extra card when the board is stable.
card_roles.Takenuma, Abandoned Mire: A Swamp that channels back a fallen creature — cheaper for each legendary you control — recovering a combo half or lord after removal without ever being a dead draw.
card_roles.Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth: Every land becomes a Swamp — the patch for a manabase carrying 49 black pips across 35 black spells. Your painlands and white sources all tap for black under it.
card_roles.Agadeem's Awakening // Agadeem, the Unde: A black land (pay 3 life or enter tapped) that hides a mass reanimation X-spell — the single best post-sweeper rebuild card in the deck, returning a stack of different-cost Vampires at once.
card_roles.Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid: A tapped black land that can instead be cast to trade a spare token for two cards — then played as the land from exile later. Both halves fit a deck rich in expendable bodies.
card_roles.Plains: The lone white basic — the Prismatic Vista and Path to Exile target.
card_roles.Swamp: Four copies: the fetchable, Urborg-independent backbone of a 49-black-pip manabase.

mulligan:
Run the engine-hand test the strategic frame prescribes: your enablers are cheap Vampire spells and your payoffs are lords and drain pieces — keep enabler-heavy hands, ship payoff-heavy ones. Concretely, keep two to four lands (the goldfish's own mulligan rule keeps 2-5, and 81.4% of first sevens pass; kept hands cluster at 2-4 lands) plus at least two Vampires you can cast in the first three turns. Those casts are worth double — a body and an eminence token each — and the payoffs find themselves: a lord or Vampire payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 67.7% of games and a drain engine in 62.5%, so you never need to mulligan toward them.

Never keep a hand for Edgar and never mourn his absence — he lives in the command zone, and the engine runs at full power while he sits there. Ship: zero-or-one-land hands, five-plus-land hands, and any hand whose spells all cost four or more, which does nothing for three turns in a deck built to bank a token per turn from turn one or two. One nuance from deck-facts: 16 of the 34 lands can enter tapped, so a two-land keep wants at least one land that comes in untapped for the one-drop start. Protection (held by turn 6 in 57.1% of runs) and a tutor are luxuries in an opener, not requirements — the free mulligan exists, and this deck at six cards with a working curve beats seven cards of top-end every time.
upgrades:
The bench for this deck is not an upgrade queue — it is a 36-card sideboard the pilot owns in paper, and its full swap analysis runs as its own department from the sideboard artifact. What belongs here is the shape of it. The largest coherent package is aristocrats: Viscera Seer, Cruel Celebrant, Indulgent Aristocrat, Blood Petal Celebrant, Gluttonous Guest, Wedding Security and friends would lean the deck into sacrifice loops that the maindeck's Grave Pact and eminence tokens already half-support — a real identity shift, not a power patch. Above that sit the standalone heavy-hitters: Elenda, the Dusk Rose (a death-triggered token army), Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet (exiling graveyard-hungry opponents' creatures while growing), Purphoros, God of the Forge (2 damage to each opponent per body — every eminence token becomes a Lava Spike), and Herald's Horn for cost reduction plus card flow.

One bench card deserves a precise note: Sanguine Bond. Its oracle text — 'Whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life' — is word-for-word Vito's first ability. That means it slots into Vito's side of the verified loops, pairing with Exquisite Blood or Bloodthirsty Conqueror as a redundant third copy of the drain half; it does NOT combo with Vito himself, whose trigger it merely duplicates. Structurally these pairings mirror stacks 001 and 004, but neither Sanguine Bond line has its own checker-passed stack, so treat them as strongly indicated rather than verified. Finally, four bench slots are spares, not options: a second Strefan, a second Vito, and two printings each of Vampire Nocturnus and Unholy Officiant — backup copies of cards the deck already runs or cut, sitting in the box.
threat_assessment:
You do not get a quiet game. Edgar Markov is one of the most famous commanders in the format, and a bracket-4 table reads your deck from the moment your commander is announced: eminence tokens from turn 1 make 'I haven't done anything' unsellable, because every cheap Vampire you cast visibly banks a body (goldfish: 1.9 bodies by turn 3, 4.2 by turn 6 with zero mana spent on the commander). Your perceived threat updates every cast, so your deflection budget spends down fast — plan the pivot before it's gone, not after.

What gets answered first, in order: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose dies on sight. Both of the deck's contained infinites route through him (Exquisite Blood + Vito, popularity 107,037; Bloodthirsty Conqueror + Vito, 64,824), and at a bracket-4 table everyone knows it — the strategic frame is blunt that opponents will play against the loop even though natural assembly is only 2.8% by turn 6. Second: the drain engines (Sanctum Seeker, Bloodletter of Aclazotz) once anyone does the stack-003 math — seven attackers is 14 life from each opponent at declare attackers, before a point of combat damage. Third: Grave Pact and the doublers draw enchantment removal from anyone who has it. The lords mostly survive; they're the wrong things to protect anyway.

Sequencing to protect the two-card kills: the tutors are your concealment. Demonic Tutor and Vampiric Tutor put the missing half into hidden zones — the table knows what a tutor with Vito on board means contextually, but they cannot see the card, and Exquisite Blood in hand cannot be answered. So never present the pair in the same open-mana window: land the half the table undervalues first (Exquisite Blood alone reads as a lifegain trinket; Vito alone is a 3-mana creature they may not want to spend real removal on), and complete it the turn the answer-holder is tapped out or has just spent the wrath. Prefer the enchantment half when interaction is up — stack 004's honest finding is that the Conqueror loop offers a removal window every iteration because the gain half is a creature, while stack 001's loop only needed Vito to survive one window.

Edgar himself: keep him in the zone. The engine is free from there (his eminence ability states its zones and functions from the command zone — CR 113.6b), and goldfish says the honest cast is late anyway: mean 6.613, median 6, only 52.1% castable by turn 6 on 5.36 mean mana. Cast him the turn he converts the board — haste plus the attack trigger (+1/+1 counter on every Vampire) turns an accumulated token board into an alpha strike — and note that resolving him flips on your free protection suite: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat cost {0} only while you control a commander. Cast Edgar = swing wide with a free indestructible effect held. That is the turn to embrace archenemy: you are already the threat by construction, so take the label on the turn it kills a player, not a turn earlier.
matchups:
VS SWEEPER CONTROL: Assume the wrath — over four players one is near-certain — and let eminence be the rebuild: every post-wrath Vampire cast re-banks a token with no recast tax, and Bloodghast returns on a land drop for free. Deploy in waves ('commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further' — strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math), and time your commitment turns to protection, which the goldfish says you hold in 57.1% of games by turn 6. The one thing you cannot rebuild cheaply is a died Edgar: he re-enters the zone but the next cast is 8 (CR 903.8), so the free Flawless Maneuver window that his presence enables is precisely for the turn you commit. Your own Olivia's Wrath is asymmetric (-X/-X to non-Vampires) — against a creature-heavy control shell it is a second alpha strike.

VS LIFEGAIN HATE: Know exactly which half of your deck dies. A 'players can't gain life' effect turns off both infinites (each loop needs your gain to convert into their loss) and blanks the lifelink bodies — but the combat drain plan is life LOSS, not lifegain: Sanctum Seeker's opponent-loss trigger and Bloodletter's doubling still function, so the stack-003 arithmetic (7 attackers = 14 per opponent at declare with Bloodletter out) is fully intact. Against hate pieces, stop tutoring for Exquisite Blood and start tutoring for the hate's answer or for Bloodletter; the drain engine was drawn by turn 6 in 62.5% of goldfish runs, so the fallback plan is the plan you usually have anyway.

VS STAX: You are the forced beatdown. The 19+19 two/three-drop core is exactly the many-cheap-spells profile that Sphere effects halve, and your mana is already tight — 16 of 34 lands enter tapped, land-drop rate falls to 59.2% by turn 6, and mean available mana is 5.36 on turn 6. Race the lock's assembly: one stax piece is an inconvenience, the layered second and third are the lock, so identify which piece beats YOU specifically (usually the tax on casts, since eminence pays per cast) and aim Despark/Fracture/Rite of Oblivion at that one. Edgar stays zoned longer here — 6 mana plus tax under a Sphere is a turn you don't have.

VS FASTER COMBO: Your combat clock does not beat a tuned combo turn — commander mean cast 6.613, mean bodies 6.36 by turn 10 — so answer economy inverts: the last profitable moment for held interaction is now. The white removal and Deflecting Swat are the cards that matter, with the standing tension that Swat is free only once Edgar is out — against a known combo seat, that is a real argument for an earlier, unprotected Edgar cast purely to turn the free interaction on. Your counter-clock is the tutored Vito line: 2.8% natural by turn 6 is not a plan, but Demonic/Vampiric/Diabolic Intent make it a two-turn threat, and stack 001 verified the kill is a deterministic full-table loop (38 iterations, retargeting each trigger) once it goes unopposed.
